growth_story.headline: Libya's income per person rises and falls with its oil output; growth since 2017 has not won back the levels it had before 2011.
growth_story.arc: Libya's income per person has moved with its oil output, and since 1990 it has passed through four eras. It shrank by 0.1 percent a year in 1990–1999, then grew by 3.3 percent a year in 2000–2007, as activity picked up after UN sanctions were lifted in 2003 and a large public investment program drove growth outside oil and gas. In 2008–2016 it fell by 1.4 percent a year: the 2011 revolution shut down most oil output and cut income per person by 49.1 percent, and after a 91.8 percent rebound in 2012 the state fragmented and income per person fell again in 2013 and 2014. Since 2017 growth has averaged 3.7 percent a year as oil output recovered, but with sharp swings, from a 30.4 percent fall in 2020, when an oil blockade hit, to a 12.2 percent rise in 2025. Even so, income per person in 2025 was 57.0 percent below its 1979 peak and about where it first was in 1965.

threads.title: Growth follows the oil fields
threads.text: Libya's output rises and falls with oil production, which has swung sharply since 2011. An oil blockade and lower oil prices brought the 30.4 percent fall in income per person in 2020, and higher oil output lifted it by 12.2 percent in 2025.

threads.title: Rival authorities, rising spending
threads.text: Libya has been governed by rival authorities with parallel budgets, which the World Bank says has weakened fiscal discipline. The IMF describes public spending that has grown beyond sustainable levels, and it names further uncontrolled spending and political fragmentation as the main risks.

growth_story.tension: The sources describe a strong, oil-led rebound, and the data agree that growth has sped up, from -0.1 percent a year in 2006–2015 to 3.0 in 2016–2025. But the data show this mostly as lost ground being won back: income per person in 2025 was still below its level in every year from 2005 to 2010, 57.0 percent below the 1979 peak and about where it first was in 1965.
